summary: Shwe Zan Aung worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a B.A. from the University of Yangon (~1887–1891) and studied under traditional teachers U Gandama and Ledi Sayadaw in 1895.

Shōdō Harada is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Shofuku-ji under Mumon Yamada (~1962–1982), whom he succeeded, became Abbot at Sōgen-ji in 1982, and founded the Tahoma Sogenji Zen Monastery in 1995.
Shōkō Kabutogi was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Rissho University from ~1932 to 1936 and later served as a professor there from ~1968 to 1980.

Shōren Ihara was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as assistant professor at Kyushu University (attested 1959–1965, 1977) and was a member of the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 1996–1998).

Shōshin Ichishima worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served at Taisho University as Dean of Academic Affairs (attested 1983) and later Professor Emeritus (attested 2014), and was a visiting lecturer in Tibetan Buddhism at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.

Si Ti La is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Acharya Nagarjuna University under doctoral supervisor J. Sitaramamma (attested 2014). They also studied under multiple traditional teachers, including Sayadaw U Kundala and U Sajjanasāra.

Sibani Das Gupta worked in Indology. She studied at the University of Dhaka, under teacher Rajendra Chandra Hazra, and completed a doctorate at the University of Calcutta under Sushil Kumar De by 1954.

Sibaraj Chetry works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Sibnath Sarma and several teachers, and served as Lecturer of Philosophy at North Lakhimpur College (attested 2012).

Sidney Lee was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at the City of London School and Balliol College, Oxford (~1878–1882), and later held a post at Queen Mary University of London (~1913–1924).
Siegfried Goldschmidt studied under Rudolf von Roth from ~1864 to 1867 and attended the University of Tübingen in 1867.

Siegfried Lienhard was an Indology scholar who earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Vienna and completed his Habilitation at Stockholm University. He was professor of Indology at Kiel University (1962–1968) and Stockholm University (1968–1990).

Siegfried Samson Goldschmidt was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig, Berlin, Göttingen, and Tübingen (Ph.D. 1867) under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth. He became an assistant professor at the University of Strasbourg in 1881.

Siglinde Dietz worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of Bonn under Michael Hahn by 1980 and held a post at the University of Göttingen (attested 1990).
Signe Howell studied at SOAS University of London (~1972–1974) and the University of Oxford (~1975–1980). She was appointed Professor at the University of Oslo in 1989.
Signe M. Cohen is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Ludo Rocher. She holds a post as Professor at the University of Missouri.

Silvia Luraghi is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. She studied at the University of Turin (~1977–1982), where she later worked (~1992–1998), and held posts at Università degli Studi Roma Tre (~1998–1999) and the University of Pavia (~1999).

Silvio Vita was a scholar in Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and Princeton University. He held posts at L'Orientale (1992–2001) and directed the Italian School of East Asian Studies (~2001–2023).

Simo Knuuttila was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki (1976), where he served as Professor from ~1981 to 2014, and held a post at the Academy of Finland (1994–2004).

Simo Parpola is a scholar of linguistics and Assyriology who earned his PhD at the University of Helsinki (1961–1968). He held posts at Heidelberg, Chicago, and served as professor at the University of Helsinki beginning in 1978.
Simon P. James works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Durham University as Tutor in the Department of Philosophy (attested 2001) and Lecturer in Philosophy (attested 2013–2014).
